summary: The Network Information Center explains why it favors standard host names and what a good scheme should do. It suggests names made of a site part and a host part separated by a delimiter, easy to remember, and at least eight characters long. It was replaced by RFC 273.

eli5.summary: The information office says it wants everyone to use one naming style for computers and lists the things a good naming system needs. It later gave a new plan.

questions: host naming scheme site and host
subtitle: Rules for naming computers on the network

tldr.problem: Early ARPANET sites used different names for the same computers, making communication confusing. The Network Information Center needed standardized naming.
tldr.mechanism: The NIC proposed that host names should have two parts—site and host—separated by a delimiter, use memorable organization names rather than computer model names, be at least eight characters including the delimiter, and allow all sites to truncate and still maintain uniqueness.
tldr.outcome: The NIC recommended a naming standard to help network users find computers consistently across the ARPANET.

today: RFC 237 is historic and was replaced by RFC 273. The naming scheme proposed here influenced later ARPANET naming conventions and eventually the Domain Name System (DNS) that the modern Internet uses.

sections.title: The Need for Standard Names
sections.content: RFC 237 explains why the Network Information Center (NIC) favors standardized host names on the ARPANET. Different sites use different names for the same computers, which confuses users who read documents from the NIC and then try to connect using names they learned elsewhere.
sections.eli5: When each computer had lots of different names, people got confused about which computer was which.

sections.title: The NIC's Naming Scheme
sections.content:
The NIC proposes a two-part name structure: a site name and a host name, separated by a delimiter such as a dash (e.g., MIT-MULTICS). Names should be meaningful, referring to the organization and its system rather than the computer model, since computers change but organizations persist.

The scheme recommends at least eight characters including the delimiter. The site name should be a maximum of six characters, and host names should be unique within their site in the first six characters. This allows sites with only four-character tables to accept user input and truncate it while maintaining uniqueness.
sections.eli5: Names like "Stanford-AI" or "MIT-Multics" tell you both where the computer is and what job it does. The NIC likes at least eight letters so there is room for both parts.

sections.title: Role of the NIC
sections.content: The NIC proposes that once the Network Working Group sets a standard syntax and names, the NIC should be responsible for maintaining the standard and assigning names to new hosts. This includes assigning names to NIC stations and individuals in organizations not yet on the network who need to participate in network dialogue.
sections.eli5: The NIC would keep a master list of all the names and make sure no two computers got the same name.
